parole.testo: Disputed. Perhaps from Late Latin setula, diminutive of Latin sēta, saeta (“thick hair”) (compare Italian setola (“bristle”)), but the initial and the liquid would be irregular. Anders proposes a source in Vulgar Latin cirra (“lock, tuft of hair”), from Latin cirrus, influenced by saeta. Also compar

Inherited from Old Spanish mórdago, further derivation uncertain. * Perhaps derived from Latin mordicus (“biting”). * Perhaps derived from Old Basque *muir-tako (literally “for mistletoe sap”). Compare modern Basque mihura (“mistletoe”) and mihurtu (“to grow seeds”).
Inherited from Vulgar Latin *sevandīlia, possibly of Basque origin. Compare Portuguese sevandija.
